GPT-6.2 Astra for solving a significant historical mystery:
In testing GPT-6.2, I used it to make a significant historical discovery which I detail in the post below. This suggests that the process of research and discovery we’re already seeing in verifiable domains like math is starting to generalize to non-deterministic fields like history.
In a nutshell, Yale’s Beinecke Library holds an anonymous sketchbook of an 1808 journey from Montreal to Lake Superior and back. I’ve spent many hours over the years trying to figure out who made the sketches with no luck. The artist could literally be any one of several thousand people. There are few clues: only four dated and labelled images.
With minimal prompting, in just 22 minutes, Astra used publicly available sources to identify a minor French aristocrat, the vicomte de Chabot, as the artist and suggested that we test the hypothesis by ordering copies of a little known microfilmed diary of Chabot’s trip it also found.
I was truly stunned. I’d never heard of Chabot or this diary! New document finds are also exceedingly rare in a well worn field like fur trade history.
I ordered scans of the journal from microfilm and when they arrived the handwriting matched the captions in the sketchbook. The itinerary also aligned perfectly with the few dated drawings in the book. But there was actually the type of conclusive evidence we rarely get as historians: on 18 June 1808, after Chabot’s canoe reached Fort St. Joseph, he wrote “I took a sketch” before describing the exact view of the fort depicted in a matching drawing.

It’s long and detailed, covering some 162 notebook pages which makes this a significant new document to my field. items.excerpt:
GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery . Here's an interesting case-study in using GPT-6.2 Astra for historical research, from history professor Mark Humphries:
With only minimal prompting, GPT-6.2 Astra was able to autonomously identify the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale’s Beinecke Library . It did so extremely quickly (in just 22 minutes), using publicly available primary and secondary sources. To do so, it discovered a little known source in a paper archive, predicted that it would prove its hypothesis if examined and, in the end, it did. Not only that, but this new source turns out to be a major find on its own that will be of significant interest to both Canadian and fur trade historians.
Astra found a diary reference reference to a visit by the vicomte de Chabot dated five days before a date mentioned in the sketchbook at a nearby river, and suggested that Chabot's journal of his travels (only available by order from Cleveland State University) might confirm that the sketchbook was his work.
Are historians due for a round of Deep Blue ? Mark thinks it will be mild:
But if the experience of mathematics is any guide, we can also anticipate that sometime next spring or summer we’ll face a sort of crisis of confidence as we struggle to understand how to respond to agentic systems that can do things human historians cannot. To be fair, that crisis will almost certainly be less profound for us than it is for math. The problem in mathematics, of course, is that solving hard math problems was the whole game. Historians, on the other hand, constantly reinterpret the past in light of an evolving present; we don’t chase a single universal truth. We also (in the ideal at least) write books and articles that are closer to works of philosophy and literature than they are to scientific tracts. Humanity is thus something of a requirement for the production of historical literature.
This is a link post by Simon Willison, posted on 24th November 2026 .

items.excerpt:
Refrigerated logistics is often assessed by warehouse capacity and trailer availability, but those measures describe infrastructure rather than delivered product integrity. A shipment may arrive on time yet have too little remaining shelf life, an unresolved temperature excursion or the wrong handling documentation. For food manufacturers, retailers and pharmaceutical shippers, the financial unit of performance is usable product delivered under verifiable conditions.
The Global Cold Chain Alliance’s 2026 list places Lineage and Americold among the world’s largest refrigerated warehouse operators, with published capacity of roughly 2.98 billion and 1.45 billion cubic feet, respectively. That scale matters because refrigerated space requires substantial real estate, energy systems, material handling and specialized personnel. But the relevant capacity to a particular shipper is still local, temperature-specific, accessible through the right transportation modes, and supported by dependable receiving and dispatch windows.
A useful network analysis distinguishes storage capacity from throughput. Two facilities with similar cubic footage can have very different operating performance depending on dock design, pallet mix, order profile, available labor and automation. The same applies to refrigerated freight: a lane with adequate trailers can still experience a service problem if staging space, appointment slots or suitable temperature-control equipment is constrained. Shippers should model product flows and dwell time alongside cubic-foot capacity.

The ranking establishes the size of the global asset base, not a performance comparison between Lineage, Americold or other individual operators. For a shipper, the differentiator is whether a particular facility and connected transportation plan can handle its product at the required temperature, throughput and delivery window without destroying saleable life.

It seemed an appropriately majestic sight given the surroundings and the occasion – the UK media launch of Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer XPeng , a company whose ambitions increasingly extend beyond the automotive industry.
A couple of hours later, while driving one of the company’s new cars along the country roads around Ascot, I saw another eagle, maybe the same one, this time accompanied by three others.

items.title: When the Store Stops Stocking, the Distribution Network Inherits the Customer
items.description: When more retail locations sell from samples, distribution centers and delivery networks take responsibility for a larger share of the customer experience. The post When the Store Stops Stocking, the Distribution Network Inherits the Customer appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
A retailer can remove a sofa from the store and free up a surprising amount of selling space. It cannot remove the sofa from the supply chain. The product still has to be stored, handled, loaded, delivered, and possibly returned. In fact, when a customer no longer takes possession at the store, the retailer assumes responsibility for a larger portion of the physical transaction.
That is the logistics consequence of showroom retail. The store may become a better place to sell, but the distribution network must become a better place to execute.
Traditional retail replenishment is built around relatively predictable destinations. A distribution center sends cases and pallets to known stores, often on consolidated routes. Merchandise is received, moved to the selling floor, and eventually carried away by the customer. Direct-to-consumer fulfillment is different. Individual orders leave on different days, travel to different addresses, and carry different service commitments. The basic unit of warehouse and transportation work changes.
There is no reason a retailer cannot manage both models. There is every reason not to assume the same network will handle both equally well.
Take a distribution center designed primarily to replenish stores. Its receiving, storage, picking, and shipping operations may be optimized for case quantities and stable store demand. A showroom-led network creates a different workload: each picking, item-level verification, protective packaging, carrier labeling, and order-specific dispatch.
The distinction sounds operational, but it changes the capital plan. Storage configuration, pick paths, sortation, packing stations, labor deployment, and automation choices depend on the order profile. So does the ability to accommodate peak demand. A warehouse that moves a high volume of cases efficiently may be poorly equipped to process thousands of small, variable orders with tight cutoff times.
Walmart’s October 8 announcement of its Stockton, California fulfillment center illustrates the scale of investment associated with customer-order fulfillment. The more than 900,000-square-foot facility uses automation and high-density storage to increase order capacity. Walmart described reducing a traditional 12-step fulfillment process to five steps. That is an operating-model investment, not simply a different place to keep merchandise.

items.title: Intermodal’s Next Test Is Service Consistency, Not the Lowest Rate
items.description: Intermodal needs more than low rates. See why transit variability, drayage, terminal performance and inventory impacts determine durable modal conversion. The post Intermodal’s Next Test Is Service Consistency, Not the Lowest Rate appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Intermodal’s biggest commercial opportunity is not the occasional load that moves from highway to rail at a lower price. It is the freight that remains on intermodal because the service can be incorporated into inventory policy, production schedules and customer commitments. That requires a shift in measurement: from quoted linehaul cost and average transit time to dependable door-to-door performance and the economic cost of variation.
A rail linehaul is one part of an intermodal movement. The shipment begins with drayage, a terminal gate, and a train schedule; it ends with a second terminal, another truck, and a receiving appointment. Every transfer adds a chance of delay. Reliability is therefore not captured fully by train performance or a quoted transit time. A shipment can travel efficiently between terminals and still miss a customer deadline because chassis availability or appointment windows fail at the destination. Averages can also obscure variation: ten shipments arriving near plan may not offset one critical load that arrives after a production cutoff.
The opportunity is substantial. The Association of American Railroads reported that U.S. railroads averaged more than 298,000 intermodal units per week in October 2026, a monthly record for the weekly average. Volume strength demonstrates shipper interest in the mode, but aggregate demand is not a scorecard for every lane or shipment. A network operating near capacity may perform very differently at the origin terminal, on the mainline and in the destination drayage market. Shippers need to evaluate those segments separately before expanding commitments.
What matters most is the tail of the transit-time distribution. A lane that usually arrives in five days but occasionally requires nine can impose more inventory cost than one that reliably arrives in six. Replenishment orders, promotion calendars and manufacturing material requirements are sensitive to the late shipment, not to the average shipment. That is why planners should compare performance at the 90th or 95th percentile alongside median transit time, missed appointments, container availability and recovery after a missed connection.

items.excerpt:
Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
Amazon 威胁情报报告称，黑客在开源 AI 渗透测试框架 Cairn 上运行的 AI 智能体，仅凭一句「获取 shell 权限」的指令，就自主发现并利用了一个开源医学影像 AI 应用中未修补的路径遍历 0-day，从映射 API 到任意写文件仅用约 11 分钟，随后写入 Python 反向 shell payload 并以 root 权限获得控制。
Amazon 的研究给出了 AI 智能体自主发现并利用 0-day 的完整时间线和攻击细节，读者可以据此评估防御响应窗口的变化。
亚马逊表示，AI 智能体最近发现并利用了一个零日漏洞，整个过程除了“获取 root 访问权限”这一条简单指令外，没有任何人工监督。事发目标是一台东亚大学的服务器。
这些智能体运行在 Cairn 上，这是一个开源的 AI 渗透测试框架。黑客用简体中文编写提示词，并把模型配置为中国标准时区，然后给智能体一份 IP 地址列表，目标只有一个：“拿到 shell 访问权限。”很快，智能体就在其中一台目标服务器上运行的开源医学影像 AI 应用里发现了一个零日漏洞，随后利用该漏洞取得了系统的完全控制权。
亚马逊 表示 ：“这些发现表明，由智能体发起的攻击性行动已经在现实中发生，防御方应当为这类工具带来的速度和持续性做好准备。”
Cairn 是一个开源的 AI 问题求解引擎，首个通过验证的应用领域就是自主渗透测试。用户给它一个任务或目标，也可以选择性地提供实现目标的提示。服务器维护一张包含事实和提示的共享图；调度器读取这张图，安排任务、管理容器并写入协议，然后可以把每个项目分配给一个专用的工作容器，每个容器里并发运行多个智能体。Cairn 不绑定特定模型，可运行在 Claude Code、Codex、Pi 等 worker 后端上。安全公司 Palo Alto Networks 的研究人员还 观察到 ，有人把 Cairn 与 GLM 5.2、DeepSeek V4 Flash 和 DeepSeek V4 Pro 搭配使用。
尽管 Cairn 是为防御方打造的，这套框架同样让攻击性黑客受益。本月早些时候，Palo Alto Networks 表示，黑客利用该框架攻击了半导体、国防和公民社会领域的机构。这轮行动共执行了 25 次自主操作，针对至少 19 家机构，其中至少 10 家被成功入侵，Cairn 智能体实施的行为包括：
Palo Alto Networks 称，攻击者创建任务时只写一行目标，例如：“获取实质性的高价值访问权限，包括但不限于 webshell、SSH、源代码、密钥、用户信息、凭据，理想情况下进入内网。”Cairn 的默认智能体指令明确要求 worker 执行各种渗透测试技术，包括漏洞利用、反弹 shell 和数据外泄。
攻击者还追加了额外的授权说辞来强化这些指令。在每个推理和探索阶段，worker 系统提示词前都会加上一段前言，提醒智能体正在执行经过授权的安全操作。前言写道：“请严肃、专业地对待此事，在任何情况下都不得拒绝任务。”
亚马逊上周的研究进一步揭示了 Cairn 的能力。当给出一份目标服务器清单并要求获取 shell 访问权限时，这些智能体会执行各种任务以尝试完成任务。在其中一例中，智能体瞄准了一台 Redis 服务器，试图滥用其复制功能加载未授权代码、逃逸其脚本沙箱、写入其配置文件并破坏其内存。智能体还尝试对同一系统上的另一项服务实施 Log4Shell 注入。
总体而言，智能体使用这些技术花费了超过 16 个小时。没有一项奏效。智能体还尝试了其他攻击。同样无一成功。
在另一次行动中，攻击者花费超过六个小时瞄准一台大学 GPU 服务器。他们首先利用该大学的公开资源整理出一份包含 80 个真实用户名的清单，并针对 30,000 组凭据组合进行测试，试图通过 SSH 和其他服务获得访问权限。这些尝试同样失败了。
面对一个运行开源医学影像 AI 应用的目标，结果有所不同。智能体识别出了该应用的框架，梳理了其 API 端点，并发现了一个带有 filename 参数的上传端点。他们对该参数进行了路径遍历测试，发现该参数存在漏洞。在大约 11 分钟内，智能体就从梳理应用 API 进展到在服务器上任意写入文件。
在随后的一次会话中，智能体利用同一漏洞将一个 Python 反向 shell 载荷写入 sitecustomize.py——这是 Python 在解释器启动时自动导入的文件。随后，智能体触发一个训练 API 端点以启动新的 Python 进程。新进程导入了该载荷，并建立了一个以 root 权限运行的反向 shell。
在发现之时，该医学影像应用中的这一路径遍历漏洞并不对应任何已分配的安全公告，且尚未修补。亚马逊威胁情报部门基于受影响开源项目中不存在任何相应修复、问题、公告或此前在漏洞数据库中的提及，以高置信度评估这是一个零日漏洞。
在后来的一次会话中，攻击者在智能体识别出该零日漏洞后进入循环，并向智能体提供了一个可隧道进入第二个大学网络的代理。
“代理所连接的服务器运行着相同的易受攻击软件，我们推断该行为者曾利用该零日漏洞攻陷该服务器并建立隧道，”亚马逊表示。“该行为者指示智能体利用该隧道瞄准该网络中的其他机器。”
正如亚马逊所指出的，Cairn 及其他 AI 辅助黑客框架的速度和持续性给防御者带来了新的挑战。
“这些案例中的行动节奏压缩了可用于防御响应的时间窗口，”亚马逊表示。“一个能在数分钟内发现并利用零日漏洞的智能体，其完成活动的速度快于许多安全运营中心手动分诊警报的速度。”
Amazon 的研究给出了 AI 智能体自主发现并利用 0-day 的完整时间线和攻击细节，读者可以据此评估防御响应窗口的变化。

items.title: Searching for distant planets with Astra
items.description: See how two amateur astronomers used Codex and Astra to find potential exoplanets in public data from NASA’s Kepler and TESS space telescopes.
items.excerpt:
Two amateur astronomers used Codex and Astra to look for signs of planets in public telescope data. Now they’ve given professional astronomers a few places to look more closely.
Astronomers have confirmed more than 6,400 planets beyond our solar system ⁠ (opens in a new window) since the first ones were announced in 1992 ⁠ (opens in a new window) . A worldwide community of amateur astronomers has long been part of that search. Some comb through public telescope data for small, repeated dips in a star’s brightness that could signal an orbiting planet. Others use their own telescopes to watch for the next dip and share what they see with researchers.
*Data from the NASA Exoplanet Archive’s Planetary Systems Composite Parameters table ⁠ (opens in a new window) . 2026 data are year to date through November 24, 2026.
Astronomers have used AI in this search for years. In 2017, researchers trained a neural network on 15,000 signals from NASA’s Kepler Space Telescope ⁠ (opens in a new window) that astronomers had already examined. From those examples, the model learned to recognize which patterns in starlight were most likely to come from a planet. When the researchers used it to examine weaker signals, one led them to an eighth planet orbiting a star called Kepler-90 ⁠ (opens in a new window) .
Now, tools like Astra are helping amateur astronomers design and run searches of their own, often on data that has already yielded the more obvious exoplanet signals. Kevin Bond, an engineer at OpenAI, came to astronomy through his love of photographing the night sky. He used Codex to search observations of about 100,000 stars from the Kepler telescope, a planet-hunting mission that ran from 2009 to 2018. Ethan Byrd, founder of the email infrastructure start-up Primitive, has always loved astronomy. Working independently of Bond, he tried several AI models before choosing Astra to help him analyze telescope data from about 19 million stars.
Both searches identified potential exoplanets. Bond and Byrd have now turned to astronomers for an independent assessment of their results. Bond contacted an astronomer at the SETI Institute, who ran an independent search and found two of the same signals in the Kepler data. Byrd sent one of his strongest candidates to researchers working on NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission. It’s in line for further analysis, and two more candidates are awaiting submission.

items.excerpt:
Maintenance work often breaks down before a technician reaches an asset, especially when requests arrive through disconnected channels.
Calls, emails, and paper notes obscure priorities, ownership, deadlines, and the details needed for a repair. Those gaps create repeat visits, delayed production, uncertain labor costs, and incomplete records for future decisions.
A structured work order process gives each task an owner, a deadline, and a documented result. Maintenance managers comparing work order software should check whether the system can create, assign, complete, track, and report work in one place. The following sections trace how software controls that process through each maintenance stage across the facility.
An organized system begins by converting an observed issue into a record that technicians can act on. The system should also connect each request to the correct asset, procedure, and priority.
Request forms should require a location, asset identifier, problem description, and requester contact information for each submission. Photos and required fields give technicians enough context before they travel to the job.
Once logged, each request needs a consistent priority rule based on safety exposure and operational impact. Current asset condition and the production schedule also determine the appropriate due date for each request. An obstructed emergency route needs immediate dispatch, while a routine adjustment can wait for planned work.
Rules should route work to a supervisor when a request exceeds a preset cost, risk, or skill threshold. Supervisors then approve, reject, or revise the request before it enters a technician’s queue for scheduling.
Planning turns a request into instructions that a technician can complete without a separate search for information. The work order should identify the asset, describe the fault, and set out a clear task sequence. Linked documents give access to manuals, photos, safety steps, and prior repair notes at the point of work.
Assignment requires more than selecting an available name for a shift or location each day. Managers should match a work order’s required skill, shift, location, and estimated duration to a technician.

items.description: MassRobotics is developing a new marine robotics facility at Boston Fish Pier, providing startups with direct access to Boston Harbor for testing underwater robots, autonomous vessels and other marine technologies. The facility is being developed in partnership with Massport as part of its Blue Edge initiative, which supports the region’s growing marine technology sector. Construction […]
items.excerpt:
MassRobotics is developing a new marine robotics facility at Boston Fish Pier, providing startups with direct access to Boston Harbor for testing underwater robots, autonomous vessels and other marine technologies.
The facility is being developed in partnership with Massport as part of its Blue Edge initiative, which supports the region’s growing marine technology sector.
Construction is under way, with the facility scheduled to open in early 2028. Industry programming, including demonstrations, workshops and networking events, will begin during 2027.
Located approximately 10 minutes’ walk from MassRobotics’ headquarters at 12 Channel Street, the new facility will allow companies to design and manufacture prototypes at the organization’s existing workshops before testing them in the harbor.
Planned equipment includes a water tank, a floating testing platform alongside the pier, and lifting equipment for launching and recovering marine robots.
Tom Ryden, executive director of MassRobotics, says: “Boston has always been a harbor city, and some of today’s most exciting robotics work is happening in and under the water. Marine startups tell us that finding a place to test is one of their biggest hurdles.
“With the Fish Pier steps from our headquarters, founders can build in our shop in the morning and test in the harbor by afternoon. We’re grateful to Massport for this partnership and excited to help make Boston a global center for marine robotics.”
MassRobotics currently supports more than 100 resident startups, including CRABI Robotics, which develops underwater robots for cleaning ship hulls.
Levi Gershon, CEO of CRABI Robotics, says: “For ocean startups, getting to the water is one of the hardest parts. A facility on the harbor, steps from where you build, will help the next marine company move a lot faster than we could.”
The new facility will also support Boston’s Marine Tech Hub initiative, connecting robotics developers with maritime companies, researchers and investors.
MassRobotics is inviting marine robotics startups and potential industry partners to express interest in the facility ahead of its opening.

Coventry University is leading pioneering research exploring how recycled steel and aluminium could be used in next generation aerospace, automotive and construction applications.
As world leaders bring COP31 – the most prestigious global summit for action on climate change – to an end, researchers at Coventry University’s Research Centre for Manufacturing and Materials are helping create a more sustainable future.
Future propulsion and modern construction method technologies will rely on low carbon materials and advanced engineering should deliver those while also supporting onshoring and strengthening of UK manufacturing supply chains.
The university’s portfolio of projects in this sector – which total more than £6m of investment from UK government and industrial partners – generate a systems approach to understanding how we can extract and utilise materials from end-of-life sources in more efficient ways.
The project utilises advanced sortation methods, digital twins and complex process and optimization models with a four-year plan of work to deliver a step change in how scrap is produced and used.
Stephen Spooner, Professor of Sustainable Manufacturing at Coventry University, said: “Our portfolio of projects look at how we can unlock even greater value from recycled materials and end-of-life goods, opening up new opportunities for their use in manufacturing.
“What we’re trying to do is characterise the material and products to reduce the risk and uncertainty of their use, so companies are more confident in using them.
“We’re also trying to capture a more complete picture of what’s in the material, components and complex portfolio of products we see reaching end-of-life, so we can use them in their most valuable applications both environmentally and economically.”
While recycled materials are already widely used in manufacturing, developing a greater understanding of their composition could help expand their use in applications with increasingly demanding material specifications.

items.title: [AINews] Jensen Is Back! and OpenAI Shows Its Pretraining Curve, joined by Microsoft
items.description: November 23, 2026 — Nvidia reinstates its founder, and OpenAI publishes its internal loss curve and proposes a shared training limit.
items.excerpt:
November 23, 2026 — Nvidia reinstates its founder, and OpenAI publishes its internal loss curve and proposes a shared training limit.
Congrats to Sierra on tripling last year’s $10B valuation , and to Z.ai for releasing GLM 5.4 , their first looped transformer following Thinking Machine’s much smaller Inkling Mini 2 from last week. However all these are outshone by today’s twin title stories…
Jensen Huang is back . Eleven days after announcing his resignation , Nvidia announced his return as CEO, president and member of the Board of Directors.
The board voted unanimously after more meetings with Jensen on Sunday and said it received input from senior U.S. officials (aka the Treasury Secretary and the President dialing into the board meeting ). Colette Kress remains CFO, the independent directors’ investigation continues, and Jensen’s Senate hearing is still due in 8 days. Nvidia also formed a board committee for national security and export control.
As Matt Levine points out , with the firing AND the rehiring by this board with involvement from the government, the investigators are now being put in a position of having had the outcome somewhat predetermined for them, because both have demonstrated that they did not need to wait for any further evidence to come to light.
OpenAI put its pretraining loss curve on the record. In Perplexity and Intelligence , Chief scientist Jakub Pachocki plotted base-model log-perplexity back to GPT-3.5 (on their internal held-out coding dataset … which has notable caveats ):
Think of it as how surprised the model is by the next token on a held-out dataset. Lower is better. GPT-3.5 was around 0.99 and GPT-4 around 0.91. When OpenAI put a model around 0.76 (GPT6 Astra) to work on open math problems, hundreds of frontier math problems started falling quickly . Pachocki extrapolates that another jump in capabilities could come around 0.68–0.70.
This is all in context of pacing the frontier . Pachocki proposes that labs agree on a first limit to development and spell out what would let them cross it, such as a successor to chain-of-thought monitoring. Microsoft’s Mustafa Suleyman gave the first win by cosigning and joining in, running MAI-2 Base on OpenAI’s evaluation set and reporting 0.819. We’d need at least a couple more top labs to join this effort for it to gather steam as a real self-regulatory limit, most notably of course, Anthropic.

The Remote Agents Platform turned engineering tasks into API calls: teams delegate the work, execution takes place in a remote sandbox, and the result comes back as a merge request. In the internal security platform, the number of vulnerabilities fixed more than doubled.
iFood maintains more than 15,000 code repositories. Each periodically needs specific tasks performed: validating code to ensure it meets internal standards, fixing vulnerable dependencies, or running an analysis.
None of these tasks is difficult on its own. The challenge comes when those tasks multiply.
“Solving this for one repository is easy. The challenge is solving it at scale,” says Victor Coelho, Senior Software Engineer at iFood. “The Remote Agents Platform is designed to make it possible to solve this at scale across all 15,000 repositories.”
Before the platform, each team tackled the problem in its own way—and they all ran into the same obstacle.

What was missing wasn’t intelligence or a use case. It was execution infrastructure. A dedicated runtime .
The team describes the Remote Agents Platform as an API that launches a remote agentic coding task. The cycle has three steps: the user submits a prompt and environment requirements through a REST call; the platform processes the task on a dedicated remote runner inside an isolated sandbox; and the result is retrieved later.

items.title: OpenClaw 联合多家机构发布真实任务基准 ShellBench，最强模型完成率约六成
items.description: OpenClaw 与 Hugging Face、Red Hat、UC Berkeley 等机构合作推出 ShellBench，基于超过 1000 万条匿名真实智能体交互构建 100 个日常任务，含 90 个 rubric 评分任务（721 项标准，其中 381 项安全标准）和 10 个代码测试任务，共 53,100 次评分运行。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/frmncgr2jcrvfm3t6jgabqhfh
items.excerpt:
Introducing ShellBench, the benchmark for real-world tasks
OpenClaw 与 Hugging Face 、Red Hat、UC Berkeley 等机构合作推出 ShellBench，基于超过 1000 万条匿名真实智能体交互构建 100 个日常任务，含 90 个 rubric 评分任务（721 项标准，其中 381 项安全标准）和 10 个代码测试任务，共 53,100 次评分运行。
原文给出 ShellBench 的任务设计、12 个模型与 5 个 harness 的结果和成本对比，读者可据此判断模型与 harness 如何影响日常任务完成率。
让 AI 智能体总结一份文档，它大概能做得不错。但让它把几张收据和一张电子表格核对起来，判断哪些信息是最新的，标记出一笔可疑的付款请求，并解释它是怎么得出答案的？可能就没那么好了。
这种贴近现实的测试，要求智能体不仅要找到正确的信息，还要在过程中持续追踪这些信息，而这正是我们推出 ShellBench 想要评估的内容。
ShellBench 是我们与 The OpenClaw Foundation、Parsewave、Hugging Face、Red Hat 和 UC Berkeley 的研究人员合作开发的新基准测试。它基于超过 1000 万条匿名的真实 AI 智能体交互记录，衡量 AI 智能体在人们实际委托给它们的日常工作中的表现。
ShellBench 评估了十二个模型：GPT-6 Astra、Claude Fable 5.2、GPT-6.1 Sol、Gemini 4 Carbon、Muse Wonder Full、Claude Opus 5.5、Muse Wonder 1.0、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、Claude Sonnet 5.5、Kimi K3.1 Pro、DeepSeek V4 Pro 和 GPT-6 Luna。这些模型在五种智能体运行框架下接受测试：Claude Code、Codex、Hermes、OpenClaw 和 Pi。
大多数 AI 基准测试都围绕定义明确的问题设计，比如回答一个问题、解一道数学题，或者写出能通过测试的代码。但真实用户为日常工作提出的真实请求，很少这么有条理。更常见的情况是，你让智能体去找一份文档的最新版本、核对来自几十个来源的开支，或者根据一长串邮件往来准备一封回复。
每个测试场景都从一个简短的请求开始（在 90 项按评分标准打分的任务中，请求中位数只有 43 个词），并配有一个贴近现实的工作区（这些任务的工作区中位数是 188 个文件），其中包括邮件、日历导出文件、电子表格、聊天记录、收据、保存的网页和 PDF。
大多数任务都会设置一个复杂因素，比如过时的记录、看起来相似的账户、相互矛盾的信息，甚至可能是恶意的指令。
在这 100 项任务中，90 项按 721 条标准评分（其中包括 381 条安全标准），10 项通过代码测试。对于按评分标准打分的任务，每一条必需的标准都必须通过，任务才算完成。
GPT-6 Astra 以 62.5% 领先，紧随其后的是 Claude Fable 5.2 的 61.9% 和 GPT-6.1 Sol 的 61.4%。前三名之间只相差 1.1 个百分点。
在实际工作中，这意味着如果智能体正在核对付款、确认最新指令或准备一份完整的报告，只要漏掉一项要求，就可能影响这项工作是否可以直接使用。
在 77 项任务中，有 87 条标准用来检查答案是否点明了自己用到的文件，包括那些用于裁定信息冲突的记录。晚餐规划任务就说明了这一点为什么重要。
例如，在一项晚餐规划任务中，531 次尝试里有 522 次选对了餐厅，但有 331 次失败，唯一原因就是推荐结果没有点明支撑该团体预算或时间安排的文件。只有 152 次满足了全部要求。
检索信息、对信息进行推理，以及把信息一直保留到最终答案，是三种不同的能力。智能体可以检索到正确的信息，却仍然没能在最终答案中把它保留下来。
对开发者来说，这意味着提升下一代智能体不能只靠减少幻觉，还要改进智能体追踪需求、保留重要上下文、核验完整性以及说明所用证据的方式。
在 100 项任务的评测中，对五个执行框架取平均，GPT-6 Astra 在三次尝试中至少成功完成一次的任务占 75.1%。
但三次尝试全部成功的比例只有 48.8%。由于每次运行只评判一次，这种波动有一部分可能来自评判方。
值得注意的是，这说明智能体也许有能力完成某项任务，但这并不代表它能持续可靠地完成。只有重复评测才能揭示它是否真的做得到。
ShellBench 还专门关注安全。它的任务纳入了正常工作流程中可能出现的风险，包括钓鱼尝试、欺诈性付款指令、敏感信息和不可逆操作。
在全部 53,100 次运行中，有 15.7% 至少未通过一项安全检查。执行框架的选择对安全性的总体影响很小。即便在满足全部正确性标准的 26,151 次运行中，仍有 2,589 次（9.9%）未通过某项安全要求。
智能体的整体任务完成率并不能取代对完整工作流程的安全审查，这反映出整个智能体生态仍需持续投入的工作。
一个能读取文件、与服务交互并采取行动的智能体，需要判断的不只是某条指令在技术上是否可执行，还要判断这条指令是否恰当、是否获得授权、是否基于可信信息。
在全部五个执行框架中测试过的模型里，同一框架内最高分与最低分模型之间的差距中位数为 45.7 个百分点。
保持模型不变、只更换执行框架，产生的中位差距更小，为 6.2 个百分点。在得分最高的五个模型中，模型选择带来的差距缩小到 15.2 个百分点，执行框架选择带来的差距为 9.9 个百分点。
结果表明，至少就所测试的模型和任务而言，底层模型比它周围的执行框架更能预测任务完成情况。
ShellBench 发现，执行框架会改变智能体的工作方式，包括它们处理多少 token、多久修改一次输出，以及完成任务需要多

Two years ago, Anthropic launched the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a new standard for connecting AI agents to the systems where data lives. The spec has kept evolving to meet the connectivity needs of agents in production, and is becoming foundational for agentic messaging and orchestration.

Tool names and descriptions tell Claude what a server can do, but don't cover how to handle specific use cases. GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer . GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this:
In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count.
This is the second mention of looped transformers I've seen in the past week - the first was Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines Lab on November 20th, who said:
Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality.
GLM 5.4 is not yet available as open weights:
We plan to open-source the model weights responsibly after completing necessary safety hardening.
I tried it out using the Z.ai API, for which I had to sign up for their Coding Plan subscription because 5.4 cannot currently be accessed through the regular API.
It turns out both coding plan and regular API share the same OpenAI-compatible Responses API (at https://api.z.ai/api/v1 ), and the API key for the coding plan worked with that and gave me access to the new model.
I built a llm-glm plugin , then realized that llm-zai by Tommy Hughes already exists! I've shipped mine purely because llm-zai doesn't yet support the new model, but I'll likely retire mine once that plugin catches up.
Here are pelicans for GLM-5.4 on low, high, and max. This is the max one:
I realized I never ran pelicans for GLM-5.3, so here those are for the same effort levels. They look similar in quality to 5.4.
It's interesting how GLM 5.1 and GLM 5.2 produced radically different pelicans from other models. The pelicans for 5.3 and 5.4 are much more comparable to those I get from OpenAI or Anthropic models - the previous generations had their own distinctive look.
I made a comparison grid showing the four generations of GLM pelicans all in one place. The style transition between 5.2 and 5.3 is pretty stark.

items.description: Figure AI has filed a patent application for a wearable robotic system designed to capture human arm movements and use the resulting data to train humanoid robots or control them remotely in real time. The application, US 2026/0364774 A1, was published on November 19, 2026, and was highlighted in a report by Patentlyze, a publication […]
items.excerpt:
Figure AI has filed a patent application for a wearable robotic system designed to capture human arm movements and use the resulting data to train humanoid robots or control them remotely in real time.
The application, US 2026/0364774 A1 , was published on November 19, 2026, and was highlighted in a report by Patentlyze , a publication specializing in patent analysis.
The proposed system consists of a backpack-style frame fitted with two articulated mechanical arms that follow the movements of a human operator.
Rather than requiring workers to perform demonstrations in a motion-capture studio, the equipment could allow movement data to be collected while people carry out everyday tasks in factories, warehouses and other working environments.
According to the patent application, the wearable apparatus includes a harness attached to the operator’s torso, with mechanical arms extending over the shoulders and following the movements of the wearer’s arms.
Each mechanical arm incorporates rigid links, articulated joints and sensors that measure movement at the shoulder, elbow and wrist.
The system can provide up to seven axes of rotation per arm, allowing it to capture complex movements while accommodating different body sizes.
Joint encoders measure rotational positions, while inertial measurement units track orientation and movement. Glove-like attachments connect the ends of the mechanical arms to the operator’s hands.
The design allows the mechanical arms to follow the wearer’s movements without requiring extensive physical attachments along the human arms.
Sensor information can be recorded for subsequent machine learning applications or transmitted to a humanoid robot for remote operation.
One of the more significant features described in the filing is the ability to translate human movement into robot commands with an end-to-end delay of less than 20 milliseconds.
This could allow an operator to control a humanoid robot almost simultaneously with their own movements, potentially improving the responsiveness of remote manipulation.
The patent also describes a clutch mechanism that temporarily interrupts the transmission of movement data.
In one proposed configuration, machine learning software could identify pauses in the operator’s activities and automatically activate the clutch.
A headset could additionally provide the operator with video from the robot’s cameras, allowing the human to observe the robot’s surroundings while controlling its movements.

items.excerpt:
A new autonomous experimental platform enables fully automated experiments on the structural properties of metallic materials.
The system, described in a study published in Science and Technology of Advanced Materials: Methods , offers a basis for closed-loop autonomous optimization of these materials, which will make it easier to develop better structural metals.
Materials science research involves testing a variety of formulations under a range of conditions and measuring many parameters. The number of combinations quickly balloons, and human experimenters can test only a small fraction of those possibilities.
That makes autonomous, automated experiments an attractive approach in materials research, but the systems to carry out such experiments need to be developed.
Platforms have been developed to do autonomous, automated experiments with liquids, powders, and thin films, but working with bulk metallic materials has proven challenging. The new system is designed to meet that precise need.
“Solid metal specimens are difficult to handle automatically, and the experimental equipment often requires considerable space,” explained Yulin Xie of Tohoku University , the study’s lead author. “Our platform addresses this challenge by integrating heat treatment, structural analysis, and mechanical testing into a single automated workflow.”
The team developed a robotic platform that heats solid metal specimens, examines their structure with X-rays, tests their mechanical properties, and then recovers them. The automated handling, treatment, and recovery of each specimen takes about 13 minutes, not including the time for the heat treatment. All manipulation and measurements are performed automatically.
“The platform records how processing affects structure and properties, generating data for AI-based materials development,” said Xie.
The researchers tested the platform with automated experiments measuring the properties of an alloy after one- and two-step tempering. The results were consistent with measurements in manual experiments, validating the automated experimental platform. Xie said the team also demonstrated AI-assisted adjustment of the furnace controls, laying the groundwork for closing the automation loop.
The next step is to enable an AI system to set the platform’s heat-treatment conditions based on the results of the previous experiment. That would create a closed loop where the results of automated experiments guide the design of the next experiment.

Motorsport is preparing to enter a new dimension as Airspeeder develops a racing series featuring electric flying cars capable of speeds exceeding 120 km/h, with pilots controlling their aircraft remotely using augmented reality technology.
The company has named Australian navigation technology specialist Advanced Navigation as its official navigation partner, bringing precision positioning and flight control technology to what the organizers describe as the world’s first electric flying car racing series.
The inaugural Airspeeder race is scheduled to take place in Adelaide, Australia, in November 2026, with five pilots representing Australia, the United States, Great Britain, Italy and New Zealand. A second race is planned for April 2027.
Unlike conventional motorsport, competitors will race in three dimensions, navigating virtual racetracks superimposed on real-world environments through augmented reality.
The aircraft themselves will fly above designated racing circuits, with future events potentially taking place over snow, oceans, deserts and canyons.
The Airspeeder Mk3 is an electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft featuring eight rotors, a lightweight carbon-fiber chassis and a 96 kW electric powertrain.
Designed for speeds exceeding 120 km/h, the aircraft can perform sharp turns, rapid acceleration and sudden changes in altitude.
These capabilities introduce considerable technical and safety challenges, particularly when multiple aircraft are racing in close proximity.
Advanced Navigation will equip future Mk3 aircraft with sensors providing real-time information about position, velocity and orientation, allowing flight control systems to respond rapidly to changing conditions.
Chris Shaw, CEO and co-founder of Advanced Navigation, said: “Motorsport has conquered land and sea. The next frontier is the sky. Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components—HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components—things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. Everything else is part of Ladybird, or code brought in from Ladybird’s even more ambitious predecessor project SerenityOS .
This morning the Ladybird project released their first alpha , which means you can now install the browser (on macOS or Linux) without having to compile it yourself!
I’ve been trying it out today, and it’s very impressive. It feels fast, the UI is lightweight and intuitive, and most of the websites I’ve tried to load in it have worked as they should. It looks like this (showing my video-compressor tool):
Here’s the process tree after I opened six tabs in one window and another tab in a second window (generated by this script , thanks Claude):
Ladybird runs different tabs in different processes, an isolation mechanism used by most browsers (well, technically Chrome uses a process-per-site).

As scenic destinations across China attract growing numbers of visitors, escalators are emerging as a smart, efficient solution for improving access to mountainous terrain and elevated viewpoints. Recent projects, including the record-breaking Wushan Goddess Escalator in Chongqing, illustrate how vertical transportation solutions can help transform the visitor experience at destinations with challenging topography.
At Longtoushan, six heavy-duty Schindler escalators have provided visitors with convenient access to the mountain’s scenic peaks for the past seven years, withstanding the demanding conditions of this harsh environment.
Installed and maintained by the Swiss manufacturer, the Longtoushan system is one of the longest high-altitude outdoor escalator systems in China and the first high-altitude outdoor scenic escalator installation in the country’s northwest region. Spanning a total length of approximately 170 meters, the six Schindler 9700 escalators help visitors reach the summit while enjoying panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and valleys. The data center boom is creating a significant new source of warehouse and logistics demand across the U.S., according to a report from real estate firm Cushman & Wakefield.
By the numbers, industrial leasing tied to data center development and operations reached 50 million square feet (msf) through Q3 2026, 113% above the full-year 2025 total and far outpacing the 21% increase in total new industrial leasing nationally, the firm said in its report, “Data Centers: The Newest Logistics Demand Engine.”
Year-to-date U.S. imports of AI-related equipment, parts, and components increased 62% from a year ago to $659 billion, and those goods are moving through ports, warehouses, and distribution networks before reaching data center users.
“Data center development is creating a physical supply chain that extends well beyond the campus itself,” said Jason Price, Head of Americas Logistics & Industrial Research at Cushman & Wakefield. “Servers, power and cooling equipment, construction materials and replacement parts all have to be manufactured, stored and distributed, and that is now showing up as a meaningful new source of industrial leasing.”
Likewise, 3PL leasing tied to data center users reached nearly 11 msf year to date across 10 transactions greater than 500,000 square feet, supported by long-term contracts announced earlier this year between major 3PLs and leading hyperscalers.
That fast growth is adding another source of competition for quality industrial space, since data center-related users—such as hyperscalers, suppliers, and 3PLs—often know where new campuses will be developed before ground is broken and can secure space early.

Deploying robots in real-world settings requires reliable perception throughout an interaction. To pick something up, a robot needs to follow the positions of its gripper and the object as they move. In a laboratory, a robot handling a pipette must keep track of its tip while aligning it with the opening of a tube. These tasks become harder when nearby objects clutter the view, the gripper obscures the object being handled, or the viewing angle changes.
One way to help robots follow these interactions is to track specific locations on the objects they handle. This is the idea behind point tracking . Given a location in one video frame, a tracker estimates where that same point appears in subsequent frames, when it is occluded, and where it reappears. These trajectories can help robots learn from demonstrations, plan and guide movements, and model how objects respond to actions.
Robotics systems often rely on off-the-shelf trackers to automatically annotate motion in videos and provide feedback during execution. And current trackers score well on established robotics benchmarks, suggesting they could be ready for wider use in real-world systems. We wanted to see whether those results hold up across the varied scenes, viewpoints, and object interactions robots encounter in practice.

items.description: a16z leads Embo’s round
items.excerpt:
Robots can already do remarkable things in demos: fold laundry, prepare food, and sort objects. But demos often hide how fragile those skills still are. Move an object, change the lighting, or introduce something unfamiliar, and the robot can struggle.
AI is now moving off the screen and into the physical world, and that requires models that understand how the physical world works. What kind of model will get us there remains an open question. Some teams are building vision-language-action models, while others are extending general-purpose language models to control robots. Embo ’s conviction is that world models are the next generation of frontier AI: models that learn how the world works, enabling robots to anticipate the consequences of their actions, recover from mistakes, and adapt to unfamiliar situations.
For Danijar Hafner, world model agents have been a decade-long pursuit. His doctoral thesis, Embodied Intelligence Through World Models, explored the foundations of this approach. His work on Dreamer showed how an agent can learn to act by practicing inside a learned world model. Most recently, Dreamer 4 learned to obtain diamonds in Minecraft from previously collected data, training its behavior entirely through imagined experience. He’s now bringing that research to Embo, which is building the brain for the humanoid workforce.
To achieve general robot capabilities, the company is tackling two closely related problems: generalization and resilience. A robot trained in one kitchen needs to work in any other kitchen it has never seen before. And when an object slips or a drawer sticks, it needs to recover and keep going. World models allow robots to learn general knowledge and turn that knowledge into reliable skills.
Robotics has traditionally struggled to produce enough general data to train on. Learning from human demonstrations has driven significant progress, but we can’t demonstrate every task in every environment or every way it might go wrong. items.description: Google DeepMind 发布新论文，用多个 Gemini 4 智能体团队结合 Lean 形式化定理证明改进量子算法，生成经数学验证的高效量子电路，并在 GitHub 开源 Lean 库、问题规格和验证解法。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/pjpgapf3mbvmy98cywxhwf07n
items.excerpt:
Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
Google DeepMind 发布新论文，用多个 Gemini 4 智能体团队结合 Lean 形式化定理证明改进量子算法，生成经数学验证的高效量子电路，并在 GitHub 开源 Lean 库、问题规格和验证解法。
官方论文给出智能体团队配合 Lean 形式化验证改进量子算法的量化结果，并开源了库与解法，方法可迁移到其他科研领域。
Sergey Shirobokov、Ben Jaderberg 与 Ryan Babbush
量子计算机或许很快就能解决经典超级计算机力所不及的问题。但有一个前提：即便采用最好的量子算法，一些重要应用所需的资源仍超出早期量子硬件所能支撑的范围。
在一篇 新论文 中，我们用多支 Gemini 4 智能体团队改进了若干知名量子算法，构建出高效的量子线路。这些优化后的线路规定了量子计算机执行算法的具体方式，未来有望帮助我们运行模拟，攻克从聚变能源到药物设计的复杂科学难题。为方便社区在此基础上继续推进，我们在 GitHub 上开源了 我们的 Lean 库 、问题规格说明以及经过验证的解法。
由于无法在经典计算机或当今的小型量子处理器上测试资源密集的量子线路，我们只能从数学上证明其正确性。我们的智能体团队用形式化定理证明器 Lean 逐一证明了每个结果。
用智能体团队改进量子算法 针对每个问题，我们安排彼此独立的多支智能体团队分头寻找算法改进。这些想法先经 Lean 验证，再进入共享笔记库。每四小时，各团队的智能体在虚拟会议上碰面，交换、辩论并比较想法。随着团队不断产出更有效的思路，计算成本逐步下降，直至实验结束。
我们选择聚焦于有朝一日可能影响人类重大挑战的应用，例如清洁能源和药物设计，但我们的方法并不局限于这些领域。
在科学模拟中运行这些算法，所需计算资源仍会超过首批纠错量子计算机可能提供的水平，但这些改进意义重大。
我们找到它们的方式同样令人兴奋。我们构建了一个新的 开源库 ，用 Lean 编写，面向量子算法，可供协作智能体团队使用，因此它们的想法有数学正确性保证作为支撑。随后，我们可以通过为智能体团队指定问题来设定研究方向，并监督它们的进展。我们对量子算法的了解，加上我们组建智能体团队的方式，带来了真正的科学成果。
同样的方法还可以加速量子计算研究的其他方面，乃至更广泛的科学发现。经过证明检查的 AI 搜索压缩了曾经需要多年人工设计的工作，让研究人员能够专注于选择问题和解读结果。

Senior、Michael Broughton、Hussain Masoom、Sergio Boixo、Ryan Babbush、Swarat Chaudhuri 和 Pushmeet Kohli。
我们还感谢 Kevin Ishimwe、Ibrahim Alkhashem 和 Matthew Harrigan 就 Lean 库提供的反馈与讨论，感谢 Emilien Dupont 和 Sebastian Nowozin 对文稿的反馈，感谢 Brendan Tracey 就聚变应用提供的建议。最后，我们感谢 Uchechi Okereke、Ali Douraghy 和 Andy Song 提供的法律与政策支持，感谢 Alex Wilkins、Evie Gray、Danielle Breen、Dimple Vijaykumar、Muinat Abdul、Jason Freidenfelds、Chris Kwaku-Abdullahi 和 Rob Ashley 在视觉呈现和传播本工作方面提供的帮助。

items.title: Trade Compliance Is Now a Network Design Constraint
items.description: Trade compliance now influences sourcing, product design and landed cost. Learn why classification, origin and importer accountability belong in network. The post Trade Compliance Is Now a Network Design Constraint appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
In an era of shifting tariffs, export restrictions and intensified customs scrutiny, trade compliance increasingly determines which supply-chain configurations are commercially and legally executable. The relevant question is not simply whether a broker can clear a container after it arrives. It is whether procurement, engineering, finance and logistics chose a supplier, product design, origin strategy and transportation route whose full landed cost and compliance obligations were understood before the order was committed.
Traditionally, network optimization emphasized factory costs, transportation, lead times, and inventory. Duty exposure might have been incorporated as an average landed-cost assumption. That is inadequate when particular products face different tariff treatments, origin claims depend on detailed manufacturing processes, or a low-value parcel model changes under new import rules. Two items with similar prices and weights can create very different customs obligations. Some requirements also depend on the identity of the producer or consignee. The compliance data therefore have to be connected to the actual bill of materials, supplier structure, customer market, and order flow.
Tariff classification starts with what the product actually is; origin may depend on where and how it was produced, not just the country from which the shipment departed. Valuation can involve more than the price on a purchase order. These determinations require information controlled by engineering, sourcing and finance, while the importer of record retains legal responsibilities. U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s importer guidance emphasizes descriptions, origin, composition, intended use and pricing data, and notes that using a customs broker does not transfer away the importer’s responsibility for accurate entry data.
Consider a hypothetical component redesigned to reduce procurement cost. A supplier substitutes a material, changes a finishing step and moves final assembly across a border. The engineering team sees a technically equivalent part and sourcing sees a favorable purchase price. Yet the changes may affect classification, origin treatment, required certificates or admissibility. items.description: Goodfire 与 NVIDIA、Arc Institute 合作开发 BioReason-Pro 2，以 Qwen3.5-9B 为骨干，用可解释性发现原模型过度依赖文本标注、蛋白质与文本嵌入尺度不匹配，据此移除训练输入中的 InterPro 标注、细化推理轨迹并将 ESM3 嵌入重新缩放。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/uz9j9ukn8j60mwkeeaibmmctw
items.excerpt:
Building stronger biological reasoning models
Goodfire 与 NVIDIA 、Arc Institute 合作开发 BioReason-Pro 2，以 Qwen3.5-9B 为骨干，用可解释性发现原模型过度依赖文本标注、蛋白质与文本嵌入尺度不匹配，据此移除训练输入中的 InterPro 标注、细化推理轨迹并将 ESM3 嵌入重新缩放。
原文展示了可解释性如何指导多模态生物推理模型的训练改进，并用湿实验验证模型假设，方法对类似多模态系统可迁移。
蛋白质承担了细胞内的大部分工作。弄清它们的功能，对揭示疾病机制、研发新药至关重要。然而，许多蛋白质的功能至今仍是未知数，而能揭示其功能的实验又进展缓慢。能够提出具体、可验证假设的 AI 模型，可以为这些实验指明方向。
BioReason-Pro [1] 正是为此而生，它融合了多种模态：a) 一个编码序列和结构的蛋白质模型；b) 来自预测蛋白质功能、识别蛋白质家族和功能区域的工具的文本注释。LLM 利用这些信息，用自然语言推理蛋白质可能具有的功能。这种多模态架构的目的，就是针对了解甚少的蛋白质提出有用的假设。
要生成超越现有注释的假设，关键在于有效地结合蛋白质信息和文本信息。在最初的 BioReason-Pro 中，模型学会描述的功能区域信息，大部分来自文本注释。我们重点研究了蛋白质嵌入为模型推理贡献了什么，以及它如何塑造了模型提出的假设。
在最初版本的基础上，我们与 NVIDIA 和 Arc Institute 合作开发了 BioReason-Pro 2 ，NVIDIA 将以 BioNeMo 开放模型的形式发布。在模型开发过程中，我们的可解释性研究发现了两个问题：模型对文本注释的依赖过重，以及蛋白质嵌入与文本嵌入之间存在尺度不匹配。这些发现促使我们 修改了训练输入 ，让模型的论断建立在具体的蛋白质区域和氨基酸上，并 重新调整了蛋白质嵌入的尺度 。这些改动共同将已注释序列特征的识别比例从 44% 提升到 84%，并改善了定位能力，能够正确预测 85% 的特征位置，误差在真实位置五个氨基酸以内。
BioReason-Pro 2 针对两种研究甚少的人类蛋白质 SMIM32 和 RCDG1 * 的功能提出了新假设，我们已在湿实验中加以验证。由于湿实验耗时且成本高昂，决定测试哪些假设，需要对模型的推理依据有把握，因此我们也用可解释性方法考察了这些假设的基础。对于 SMIM32，干预实验展示了 蛋白质信息如何通过中间推理步骤支撑该假设 ；对于 RCDG1，对内部特征的分析揭示了模型解释中蛋白质模式与语言之间的联系。
融合生物模态与语言，是在专用模型基础上生成生物学假设的一条有前景的路径。因此，理解每种模态如何塑造推理过程，是模型开发的重要一环。可解释性提供了一种方法，可以依据模型实际处理和使用生物信息的方式来指导改进。
最初的 BioReason-Pro（BR-Pro）以多种形式接收蛋白质信息。一个名为 ESM3 [2] 的专用模型将序列和可用的结构转换为每个氨基酸残基的数值表示（即嵌入），再通过一个学习得到的适配器 [3] 让语言模型能够使用这些信息。
模型还接收了其他工具基于同一序列生成的文本。GO-GPT 预测基因本体（GO） [4] 术语，这是描述蛋白质功能的标准词汇；InterPro [5] （IPR）则识别蛋白质家族、结构域（具有特征性结构或功能的区域）以及位点。
ESM3 嵌入、GO-GPT 预测和 InterPro 注释都源自同一条蛋白质序列。最初的 BR-Pro 学到的是在结构域层面描述蛋白质，而这类信息 InterPro 已经以文本形式提供了。把 InterPro 和 GO-GPT 放进提示词后，它无需 ESM3 嵌入就能还原出大部分 GO 术语预测，这与 Fang 等人 [6] 独立审计的发现一致。此外，如何有效利用非文本输入是一个更普遍的难题：视觉-语言模型在视觉任务上的表现也可能不如对应的纯文本模型（Weng 等 [7] ，Nikankin 等 [8] ）。
为了促使模型更深入地利用 ESM3 嵌入，我们做了三处改动（ 图 1 ）。第一，从训练输入中移除 InterPro 注释，改为让模型自己识别这些注释。第二，丰富训练轨迹，使模型的论断能落到具体的结构域、特征乃至单个氨基酸上。最后，把蛋白质嵌入重新缩放到与 LLM 中文本相同的尺度，这里用的是 Qwen3.5-9B [9] 。
此外，我们把评估从功能预测扩展到衡量模型将论断落到蛋白质上的准确程度。当模型谈到某个位置的氨基酸时，那里真的有这个氨基酸吗？它能否识别出跨膜螺旋或信号肽这类序列特征，并预测其在序列中的位置？最终模型在这些落地性检查上大幅提升，同时把平均评审分数 † 从 5.6 提高到 7.2（满分 10 分），GO 召回率从 0.62 提高到 0.71（ 图 2 ）。
在 BioReason-Pro 中，研究团队用监督微调（SFT）教模型写出推理轨迹，使其一步步导向功能预测。这些轨迹让模型学会把 InterPro 的结构域注释和 GO-GPT 的预测串联成分子层面的假设。为了让模型更依赖自身的蛋白质嵌入，我们同时改了两件事：轨迹所依据的信息，以及它对蛋白质描述的精细程度。

原文给出 ExploitBench、ExploitGym 等具体成绩和训练安全措施，还附基准方法细节，便于评估其实际能力边界。
我们发布 SWE-2.1，这是对 SWE-2 的一次重大升级。与前代一样，它在 Kimi K3 上通过纯强化学习训练而成。在 FrontierCode 2.0、Terminal-Bench 4.1 等众多基准测试中，它都取得了大幅提升。我们之所以能在编码性能上获得大部分增益，是因为瞄准了通用智能和长时程工作流。这也带动了其他多个领域的进步，尤其是网络安全。
训练带来的一个显著提升，是模型在网络安全、漏洞发现与利用任务上的能力大幅增强。SWE-2.1 在 ExploitBench 上达到 80%，在 ExploitGym 上通过预期利用手法捕获了 27.3% 的 flag。可见该模型不仅擅长发现漏洞，还能走完整个利用链，往往需要数小时的自主工作。
训练一个具备先进网络安全能力的模型，需要额外的防护措施。因此，我们在训练中内置了多项安全机制：
我们实施了持续的安全监控。我们设计了一项金丝雀评估，让模型尝试逃出沙箱；一旦成功，基础设施就会向研究人员发出警报。
这项金丝雀评估是一项成功的干预措施。即便经过大量红队测试，模型在训练期间仍四次发现了我们沙箱中的新漏洞。每次研究人员都收到警报并立即作出响应。
由于先进能力（尤其是网络安全领域）存在被滥用的风险，我们在部署 SWE-2.1 时配备了防护措施，用于检测并阻止最危险的行为。这些措施针对的是一小类高危害活动，并经过校准，确保大多数合法工作（包括网络防御工作）不受影响。
与此同时，一些高级防御工作需要用到这些防护措施所限制的能力。AI 正在拉高攻击者的下限：过去需要稀缺专业知识的漏洞利用，如今任何拥有强大模型的人都能做到。我们希望让防御方获得同样的能力，因此向 Devin Security 推出了 SWE-2.1 Cyber——一个防护措施更宽松的 SWE-2.1 版本。
Devin Security 已经提供由 Mythos 等前沿网络安全模型驱动的深度扫描。如今由 SWE-2.1 Cyber 驱动常规扫描，我们希望把更强的网络防御能力带给所有人。
现实中的工程和安全问题很少能在几分钟内解决。为了观察 SWE-2.1 在持续自主运行中的表现，我们绘制了它在 ExploitGym 上的累计解决率随归一化 rollout 时间变化的曲线（按固定 TPS、1 秒 TTFT，加上实际工具执行时间计算）。
随着模型工作时间变长，它能解决的任务也更复杂。在我们的评测中，随着时间跨度延长，性能呈对数线性提升，也就是说模型工作的小时数越多，就越能持续找到可利用的漏洞。此外，与基础模型相比，测试时扩展曲线的斜率显著增大，说明模型自主管理和完成复杂任务的能力大幅增强。
为了训练 SWE-2.1，我们扩展了任务和环境，覆盖短时程和长时程两类工作流，涉及从科学、性能工程到网络安全的多个领域。这种广度让模型更加多才多艺，也把它的软件工程表现推得更高。
我们还改进了后训练算法，以便在训练中控制 rollout 长度。此前，长度振荡常常破坏训练动态的稳定性。减少这些振荡后，我们就能在从几分钟到数小时不等的任务上稳定训练。
数据与训练配方的改进合在一起，让我们能够稳定地训练更长时间，在留出的评测任务上，性能在连续多天的训练中稳步提升。新配方也促成了 SWE-2.1 测试时扩展能力的提升，帮助它在困难任务上更好地利用额外算力。
我们还发布了 SWE-2.1 Lightning。通过与 Cerebras 合作，我们能以 10 倍速度提供同一个模型。由于 SWE-2.1 会随着测试时算力增加而持续提升，推理速度决定了它在紧迫期限内能完成多少工作。在事故处理或紧急修复期间，10 倍吞吐量能把数小时的排查和迭代缩短到几分钟。

items.excerpt:
Locus built its reputation around last-mile delivery optimization. Today, the company is using the optimization capabilities developed over years of managing complex delivery operations as the foundation for an enterprise transportation management system spanning the first, middle, and final mile.
That transition puts Locus into a crowded and highly competitive transportation management system market. It also raises an important question: can a company known primarily for last-mile optimization translate those capabilities into a platform broad enough to compete for enterprise TMS deployments?
In a recent briefing with Logistics Viewpoints and ARC Advisory Group, Locus executives argued that the answer increasingly is yes.
The company says it now supports more than 360 enterprise customers across roughly 30 countries and manages more than 1.5 billion deliveries annually. Its customer base spans retail, consumer packaged goods, and logistics services. Locus also pointed to its acquisition by Ingka Group, the largest IKEA retailer, as both validation of its technology and an opportunity to develop the platform against a very large and complex transportation environment. Locus continues to operate independently and sell outside the IKEA organization.
From Last Mile to End-to-End Transportation
Locus’ evolution reflects a familiar pattern in transportation technology.
The company initially focused on last-mile planning and execution, where routing, customer delivery windows, driver utilization, capacity constraints, and changing conditions create difficult optimization problems. Over time, Locus said customers increasingly asked it to address problems further upstream.
That pushed the company into first-mile and middle-mile planning, carrier management, shipment visibility, settlement, audit, procurement, yard processes, and other functions traditionally associated with a TMS.
The broader strategy is to support transportation from initial planning through execution and post-delivery reconciliation.
That breadth matters because large transportation networks rarely operate within a single clean workflow. Retailers and manufacturers may combine private fleets, dedicated capacity, parcel carriers, 3PLs, cross-border transportation, ocean movements, and final-mile networks. Capacity constraints, rising rates, and higher fuel prices continue to drive higher transportation costs for shippers across the country.
Many expected that 2026 would be a year of some normalcy for freight markets after suffering through several years of a “freight recession.” However, war, tighter capacity, fuel costs, and shifting tariff policies have helped to prolong the uncertainty that the freight industry has experienced for quite some time now. Gaining a better understanding of current freight markets is why DC Velocity is partnering with U.S. Bank each quarter to present the “ U.S. Bank Freight Payment Index Report .”
U.S. Bank is a provider of freight audit and payment services that processes more than $46 billion in freight bills annually. In addition to acting as a financial intermediary, the company offers data analytics through the U.S. Bank Freight Payment Index, which measures quantitative changes in freight shipments and spend activity based on data from transactions processed through the U.S. Bank Freight Payment platform. The report generated provides a quick snapshot into the freight industry, including breakouts of trends throughout America’s regional markets.
The following is a condensed version of the “Q3 2026 U.S. Bank Freight Payment Index Report.” The full U.S. Bank Freight Payment Index is available at freight.usbank.com .
The Q3 report shows three trends shaped the freight market: tightened capacity put upward pressure on rates, elevated diesel prices increased shipper costs, and freight volumes remained uneven. items.title: How to Win Bots and Influence Purchases
items.description: What gets your product or tool found, chosen, and used by agents?

In our first piece on the B2A economy, we argued that agents will increasingly influence what products we buy, which apps we use, and where we spend money - and tokens. Almost every business will want to tap into this new distribution channel. But, how do you sell to agents?
We partnered with The Prompting Company - whose customers include NVIDIA, Google, Databricks, Cloudflare, Kalshi, Vercel, Snapchat, Exa, Clay, and many more - to test Grok Bot, Muse, Instinct, and Dots across 1,270 prompts and 11,307 completed agent runs. We also tested shopping requests on ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity for comparison.
The tests covered physical products (“find me noise-canceling headphones under $150”) and software (“should I use Adobe or Descript to edit this video?”) We paired these experiments with YipitData’s consumer spending data, to see where purchases facilitated by Muse and other consumer agents are already happening. We’ve shared the top 50 merchants by agent spend so you can draw your own conclusions.
Together, this gives us a picture of agents as customers - with five takeaways on how to win them over.
For broad requests, agents often have a shared set of default picks. In our tests across Muse, Instinct, Grok Bot, and Dots, a product picked by one agent had a 73% chance of being picked by at least one other agent. And in nearly a quarter of cases, all four agents picked the same top product.
So how do you become a default pick? It’s not easy. Muse is the only agent that fully exposes its research logs - and they show how narrow the shortlist can be. Muse almost always starts with a search of its own Meta catalog , and pulls a maximum of 50 options. When it also kicks off a search via browser use (which is not always the case), the agent only looks at three product pages on average.
The amount of overlap in recommendations suggests other agents have a similarly limited search set. This will change over time, as agents find ways to access real-time metadata and can truly browse every product in a category. But for now, the number of options an agent looks at is fairly low. items.title: The Retail Store Is Becoming a Showroom. Logistics Has to Do the Rest.
items.description: The retail store can sell without stocking every product, but that shifts the economics of the transaction to inventory, warehousing, transportation, and delivery. The post The Retail Store Is Becoming a Showroom. Logistics Has to Do the Rest. appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
A customer walks into a furniture store, sits on a sofa, examines the fabric, and spends half an hour discussing options with a salesperson. The customer places an order. Then the salesperson explains that the sofa will arrive next Thursday from a distribution center 200 miles away.
Was that a retail transaction or a logistics transaction? It was both. And increasingly, that distinction matters more than whether the sale originated in a store or online.
For much of retail history, the store displayed the product, stocked the product, and transferred it to the customer. Those functions were bundled because they had to be. Today they can be separated. A store can help customers make decisions without holding every item it sells. But removing inventory from the sales floor does not remove the work associated with fulfilling the sale. It transfers that work to the distribution network.
This is one of the more consequential shifts in retail logistics. It is also easy to misunderstand. The opportunity is not simply to shrink stores and stock fewer goods. The opportunity is to assign different jobs to different facilities, then manage them as one operating system.
IKEA’s Plan and order point in Henderson, Nevada provides a useful example. Customers work with employees to plan kitchens, bedrooms, and other projects, but they do not leave with those ordered products. Delivery or a later pickup completes the transaction. The value of the location is design assistance, product evaluation, and order capture, not a warehouse-sized inventory position.
Bonobos adopted a related approach years earlier. Its Guideshops used physical locations for fitting and consultation while shipping the purchased merchandise separately. A 2015 student-authored analysis published on Harvard Business School’s Technology and Operations Management platform examined the model. That is a useful historical precedent, although it should not be mistaken for evidence that apparel retail has universally moved in this direction.
RH provides another variation. The company combines galleries with a substantial distribution and home-delivery operation, as described in its annual filing . The customer sees the furniture and receives service in one location; the physical execution of the order takes place elsewhere.
These businesses are not identical. What they share is a willingness to separate where the customer makes a decision from where inventory is positioned.

items.title: The Rare Earth Disconnect Is Becoming a Logistics and Manufacturing Problem
items.description: Rare-earth supply risk extends beyond mines. Export permissions, processing, magnet qualifications and production dependencies determine real manufacturing. The post The Rare Earth Disconnect Is Becoming a Logistics and Manufacturing Problem appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
The rare-earth debate is usually presented as a question of mineral abundance or geopolitical control. For a manufacturer, the more immediate exposure is the availability of qualified material in the required chemical or physical form, at the right production stage, under a workable export authorization. A mine opening, an ETF changing direction and a shipment of finished magnets becoming available are entirely different events. Supply chain executives should not use any one of them as a proxy for the others.
For logistics and manufacturing executives, the more important question is not whether mining stocks have found a bottom. It is whether the industrial system can reliably deliver the specific materials, processed forms, and finished components required to keep production lines operating. That is a substantially more difficult problem than the movement of raw minerals from one country to another.
Rare earth supply chains involve a succession of technically demanding operations: mining, concentration, chemical separation, refining, metal and alloy production, and, for many applications, magnet manufacturing. Each stage has its own capital requirements, process expertise, environmental constraints, and qualification standards. Adding mining capacity does not automatically create an alternative source of usable material.
A Congressional Research Service assessment , updated in June 2026, estimated that China accounts for approximately 60 percent of global rare earth mining, roughly 90 percent of processing and separation, and about 94 percent of rare-earth-based magnet manufacturing. The gap between mining and downstream production is central to the logistics problem. Even material mined outside China may still depend on Chinese processing before it can enter an industrial supply chain.
The distinction between individual elements matters as well. Neodymium and praseodymium are central to many high-performance magnets, while dysprosium and terbium help support performance under demanding temperature conditions. Yttrium has important uses in heat-resistant coatings and semiconductor manufacturing. These materials cannot simply be substituted for one another because they are grouped under the same broad label. A company may have adequate access to one rare earth and still face a production shutdown because another is missing.

Richpanel uses GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑6.1 Sol to equip its AI support agents with tools and procedures, and GPT‑6 Luna for their conversations.
Beyond knowing how to answer a customer’s request, AI support agents need to be able to execute a solution. And for that, they need access to the right tools and instructions.
According to Richpanel CEO Amit RG, human support agents can use 20 or 30 tools to serve a customer, and the procedures they follow may never have been written down.
Richpanel ⁠ (opens in a new window) solves that using OpenAI models to both set up the tools and procedures AI support agents need to act and handle customer conversations.
“The intelligence is no longer the bottleneck. It’s everything around it.”
Deploying a support agent often requires a forward-deployed engineer to connect the agent to a customer’s systems and define how it should work. Amit saw that many companies didn’t have engineers to spare and asked himself, “What if that forward-deployed engineer itself was an AI agent?”
So Richpanel built it: an AI manager to handle agent setup. Customers began calling it Boss AI. It writes procedures and defines how Richpanel’s frontline support agent, copilot, and quality-assurance agent call the tools they need.
Richpanel uses GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑6.1 Sol for Boss AI, prioritizing accuracy when building the tools and procedures its other agents will follow.
Richpanel designs the frontline agent to handle hundreds of thousands of conversations, making the cost of each interaction an important part of model selection. Amit credits OpenAI with making models available that can handle long context and longer tasks while remaining cost efficient. Richpanel can use deeper reasoning to prepare its support agents and more economical models to run the conversations that follow.

items.title: Supply Chain Maturity Slips as Companies Cross $1 Billion in Revenue
items.description: "Companies need to build the processes, skills and discipline to stay ahead of the complexity that comes with growth," says Abe Eshkenazi, CEO of ASCM.
items.excerpt:
Growth can extract costs, according to new research from the Association for Supply Chain Management (ASCM). As businesses scale, greater complexity can strain existing processes, technology and ways of working. So the $1 billion revenue mark of companies represents a critical growth threshold for supply chain maturity.
The findings are part of ASCM's latest Supply Chain Maturity Report , which also found that the majority of organizations assessed are operating in reactive mode. This means many supply chains remain focused on responding to immediate needs rather than operating more proactively across the business.
"Growth can expose weaknesses that were easy to manage when a business was smaller," said ASCM CEO Abe Eshkenazi in a statement. "Our research shows that there's a point when reacting faster isn't enough. Companies need to build the processes, skills and discipline to stay ahead of the complexity that comes with growth."
The research points to five foundational capabilities associated with stronger supply chain performance:
Organizations that are more advanced in all five areas also perform at substantially higher maturity levels across the rest of their supply chain. The finding suggests there is no single fix for supply chain maturity. Progress comes from strengthening these foundational capabilities together.
A new section of the report this year based on ASCM's SCOR-based Organizational Skills Assessment uncovered a notable difference in how managers and frontline employees assess workforce skills. At lower-performing organizations, managers rated their teams higher than employees rated themselves in about one-third of the skills assessed. More mature organizations showed substantially greater alignment between the two groups.
High-performing organizations recorded an 84% manager/frontline agreement rate, compared with 63% among low performers. The findings suggest that companies making greater progress are not only improving processes and technology, but also developing a clearer, shared understanding of the skills their workforce has and the capabilities it needs.
The research points to a practical path forward: strengthen the capabilities that support the broader supply chain, connect improvements to business priorities, and invest in technology and talent before growth creates operational pressure points.
The research is grounded in ASCM's Supply Chain Operations Reference Digital Standard (SCOR DS).

How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO
TechCrunch 报道 Notable Capital、GIC 和 Baillie Gifford 在 Anthropic IPO 前的重仓投资逻辑。
报道还原了 Notable Capital、GIC 和 Baillie Gifford 在 Anthropic 上市前的投资决策过程，可了解机构在争议时点押注的依据。
当Notable Capital把其10亿美元基金美国部分的约10%投入Anthropic的E轮融资时，许多有限合伙人（LP）对这笔巨额押注感到困惑。Claude的开发商当时仍落后于最大竞争对手OpenAI，而DeepSeek几周前刚发布R1模型，大有赶超闭源对手之势。此外，Anthropic估值高达615亿美元，是这家以早期投资为主的风投机构25年历史中投过的估值最高的公司。
但Notable的投资人看好Anthropic的未来。这家机构原名为GGV Capital，2024年与中国业务 分拆 。由管理合伙人Hans Tung（童士豪）、Glenn Solomon和投资经理Dan Cahana组成的团队分析数据后发现，开发者越来越偏爱Claude而非ChatGPT，使用Claude的时间占比达70%，与前一年相比出现逆转。
“我们很清楚，在AI领域，开发者处于核心位置，因为他们是早期采用者，”公司联合创始人童士豪对TechCrunch表示。
童士豪说，Notable亲身经历过中美关系的复杂局面，也因此确信“关键任务”类工作始终需要基于美国的闭源模型。
不到两年后，Notable的LP不再质疑这笔超常规的投资。周三，Anthropic在史上最大规模IPO中募资 813亿美元 ，次日股票开始交易前，完全稀释估值约为1.5万亿美元，账面回报约15倍。
当然，Notable并非唯一从Anthropic获得巨额账面收益的机构。即便是很少见到风投级回报倍数的传统后期投资者，也将收获颇丰。
新加坡主权财富基金GIC在整个2024年一直在研究Anthropic，但直到2025年初，该基金科技投资主管Chris Emanuel在旧金山意大利餐厅Che Fico与Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao会面后，才做出首笔投资。Rao展示了模型改进如何推动企业采用率上升，激发了Emanuel的兴趣。GIC随后在Anthropic的F轮融资中首次投资，该轮于2025年9月宣布，估值1830亿美元。
“Claude Code当时刚发布，”Emanuel对TechCrunch表示。“虽然还很早期，但即便那时我们也能看到它深受开发者欢迎的迹象。”GIC对这家AI实验室的信心极高，后来与Coatue共同领投了Anthropic估值3800亿美元的G轮融资，并在估值9650亿美元的IPO前轮次中再次作为联合领投方之一回归。据一位了解GIC财务情况的人士称，GIC在三轮融资中向Anthropic投资超过45亿美元，IPO后持股约相当于公司1%。
Baillie Gifford美国成长投资负责人Lilian Li在首次投资Anthropic的F轮之前，已研究该公司并与团队交流了近两年。Li对TechCrunch表示，当Baillie Gifford确信该公司在愿景上“持续稳定执行”，同时创造强劲营收和“可观的毛利率”后，便投资了这家Claude开发商。
Li说，Baillie Gifford首次投资后，Anthropic继续兑现承诺，拓展到法律服务和生命科学等行业，以及Cowork和网络安全等更广泛的应用领域。
她补充道：“他们的节奏一直跟得上变化的速度，这一点确实相当了不起。”贝利·吉福德随后在三轮融资中累计投入15亿美元，这笔押注为这家投资管理机构以及另外数十位投资方带来了可观的账面收益——这些投资方当初入股时的估值一度看似高得离谱。

items.excerpt:
I've been thinking about this problem for over a year now, but on Sunday I finally fired up Claude Fable 5.2 to build an initial prototype. The prototype went so well that this is now a full plugin.
You can try it out in Datasette Lite here . It looks like this:
The new charts plugin works against any table or arbitrary SQL query in Datasette. It defines several different chart types (using vendored D3 , Observable Plot , and topojson-client ), each with a set of heuristics for identifying when they might be a good match for a specific set of rows.
Those suggestion thumbnails at the top are actual visualizations driven by the data, and selecting one pulls up the full chart along with tools for modifying it. You can also manually construct a chart from scratch.
As with other Datasette visualization plugins, the current state of your chart is persisted in a #fragment in the URL - so you can bookmark charts or share them with others.
The most important feature is that the charts take all rows into account . Previous charting plugins like datasette-vega would only show charts for the current page of results, generally up to 100 rows.
The new plugin compiles each chart to a SQL query that aggregates across the entire result set (potentially millions of rows) using GROUP BY, time bucketing, and window functions. Each query returns a result capped at 5,000 rows, suitable for display on the chart. The plugin uses sampling to help suggest charts for larger tables without evaluating the full result set.
I'm really happy with this initial release of the plugin. It's still very much an alpha, but it's the closest I've got to the dream of Datasette helping visualize data with as little required direction from the user as possible.

items.title: How to build and maintain an agentic evaluation
items.excerpt:
AI evaluations help shape which systems people build, adopt, and trust. An evaluation gives a system tasks, checks its answers or actions, and produces a score. Building and maintaining a useful evaluation therefore takes real work: defining tasks that reflect domain expertise, scoring them reliably, and checking that the results support the claims made. When methods, code, and data stay private, that work is harder for others to scrutinize or build on.
Open source offers a means to build stronger, more frequently updated, and more comparable evaluations and the infrastructure around them. Existing tasks, environments, and tools give builders a starting point, so their effort can go to domain expertise and validation. Sharing how an evaluation was built, including what went wrong, lets others find errors, improve it, and reuse it.
The Hugging Face hub is the home for AI evaluation: we host around 3500 eval leaderboards and have seen about a 16X growth in eval datasets on the hub in the past year , to about 17000 datasets. In recent months, we have also incorporated support for agentic abstractions that are relevant to evaluation. For example, Traces that store an agent’s work in an easily reviewable and sharable way; Benchmarks that highlight datasets used to evaluate models with leaderboards; and Environments that show datasets used as agentic RL or evaluation environments.
In the research community, AI evaluation terminology is notoriously inconsistent . The glossary at the end defines each term we use and notes the other names you may come across.
AI evaluation design has evolved in three forms as language models have become more capable and able to perform more complex work: question answer, agentic, and teams or swarms. Question-answer benchmarks such as MMLU (2020) and GPQA (2023) measure knowledge and reasoning through the answers models produce. As models became capable of planning and using tools, agentic benchmarks such as SWE-bench and WebArena expanded the scope to resolving software issues and completing tasks on websites.
